messages.author: e452970a8244a89b
messages.subject: Over/underdispersion in DISTSAMP
parts:
Hello unmarked users,
  I recently ran the goodness of fit code provided in the help file for parboot and the results were not encouraging:

                 t0       0%   2.5%  25%  50%   75%  97.5% 100%
SSE         577     426   429    449   473    486   503      503
Chisq       4797    2651 2757  2983  3155  3415 4193    4289
FreeTuke  520     454   455    479   495    505   515      520

As you can see, none of the t0 values fell within the range of test statistics from simulated data for any of the three GOF tests. 

I have run 16 different analyses (different species and/or habitats) and this appears to the be rule rather than the exception.  I wondered whether I might find better fit using a negative binomial distribution in GDISTSAMP, but for the first two species I've tried I get Hessian/nans errors even on null models (no covariates for p, phi, or lambda).  

I wonder if anyone has thoughts to share on what might be causing my problem(s) and perhaps provide a solution that is better than the one I am currently applying to the situation (alcohol).

Thanks,

Andrew Cox
Dept of Biology
University of Nebraska - Omaha

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Over/underdispersion in DISTSAMP
parts:
Hi Andrew,
I personally find that alcohol usually works ok, but gdistsamp might work too. Starting values Are important, try using values from the poison fit for different values of over dispersion and see if that converges
Andy
